title: Narration that turns to the student
statement: Whether narration before a story should ever speak to the student: one rule calls such lines filler that breaks the fiction, another keeps them as the labels that teach.
detail: The intro-video BrainLift holds two versions of its rules, and they disagree here (`downloads/BrainLift - What makes a good intro video.md`). The world-only version says fillers like "let's meet our characters" feel engaging and do the opposite, because a narrator who turns to the audience ends the fiction that the child is already inside the world (line 106), and it bans student framing such as "in this lesson" (line 950). The other says such connective lines are not padding but the labels that name what the child is looking at (line 315), lets the narrator of a short video speak to the viewer (line 341), and ends its own worked script on "As you read, notice how each place makes you feel" (line 405).
against: The world-only version calls itself internal doctrine, with no child yet observed watching one of its films (`downloads/BrainLift - What makes a good intro video.md`, line 249).
